A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same distributed ERM and CoCoA–ADMM study. Their complete main texts, figures, equations and appendices support comparison despite the changed title and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original parameter-sensitivity experiments, synthetic Ridge/Lasso simulations and SVM experiments on three real datasets.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain the original synthetic and real-data experimental results.

M1.justification: The five algorithms, their update equations and the two proximal-matrix choices are retained after reordering and iteration reindexing. The new introductory description of encoder functions does not specify a changed computational procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic IID/non-IID Ridge and Lasso problems and regularized SVMs on a1a, w8a and real-sim. The synthetic data-generation details and real-data experiments move to Appendix D in v2.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain CoCoA-PD and the four ADMM variants for Ridge, and the four ADMM variants for L1 regularization. The parameter-sensitivity comparisons also retain the same three algorithms.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, machine counts, tuning choices and round budgets match. However, v1 explicitly defines a normalized relative gap, while v2 defines an unnormalized certificate in Section 2 but continues calling experimental curves relative gaps. It is unclear whether the evaluation metric changed or only its documentation.

E4.justification: The same sensitivity sweeps, IID/non-IID comparisons and observations about instability under L1 regularization remain. Moving the real-data analysis into Appendix D does not introduce an additional robustness test or ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Matched Figures 2–4 retain the plotted trajectories, rankings and qualitative findings after panel reordering and redrawing. Figure 4 reuses the same six plot images. No experimental result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: v2 adds Corollary 2 and Appendix B.5, deriving consensus/proximal ADMM correspondence through exchanging primal and dual roles. Appendix A adds KKT and proximal fixed-point relations. The determinant-based convergence comparison in v1 is removed, while the exact and inexact O(1/T) theorems remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion strengthen the consensus/proximal relationship from structural similarity with an unresolved connection to parameter-matched equivalence. The existing CoCoA–proximal connection and tuning-performance claims remain, but the stronger equivalence claim materially expands the stated contribution.

C2.justification: v1 explicitly leaves the precise consensus/proximal relationship and its convergence implications for future study. v2 replaces that qualification with a saddle-point role-exchange explanation and removes the associated open-problem discussion. The restriction of the CoCoA equivalence to quadratic regularization remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies a Dell Latitude 7450 laptop, states that each experiment finishes within six hours, and says code is available in supplementary material. These are disclosures rather than evidence of changed execution settings. The explicit normalized experimental-gap formula from v1 is no longer provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds background references on ERM, losses, regularization and ADMM unification while retaining the existing literature base. It also explicitly positions the equivalence result as challenging the separation between CoCoA and consensus ADMM attributed to Smith et al. (2018).

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, introduces a dedicated preliminaries section, rewrites substantial explanatory passages and moves CoCoA after the ADMM descriptions. It also reorganizes the proofs and relocates data-generation details and the real-data experiment to Appendix D.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Figure 1 is redrawn in color, Figures 2–3 replace raster plots with vector graphics and rearranged panels, and Figure 4 moves to the appendix with reordered panels and a corrected caption. Table 1 is relocated.

improvement.justification: Corollary 2 and Appendix B.5 provide an explicit saddle-point transformation for the relationship that v1 left open. The new preliminaries, clearer diagram and execution disclosures also help readers assess the work. The net gain is limited by inconsistent dual-objective sign conventions between the main text and Appendix A and the loss of an explicit definition for the plotted relative gap.
